features: Clear feedback, a persistent badge, and a latest-result panel help you confirm a send without clicking again.
Add custom headers, a shared send UUID, or a small response receipt to the webhooks that need them.
Use page context, type a note, or explicitly paste into a value. Quick Send and right-click actions keep the capture close.
showcase: A place for every next step.
showcaseNote: Start with a simple template. Open advanced options when your endpoint needs more.
steps: Enter your webhook URL, choose an HTTP method, and add the parameters your endpoint expects.
Use variables for a URL, title, selection, or metadata. Save the template when it is ready.
Use the popup, choose a template from the right-click menu, or let a Quick Send rule choose on your toolbar click.
faq: Templates, rules, and settings stay in local browser storage. When you send, the configured parameters go to your webhook endpoint. The publisher does not receive, proxy, or log those requests. The receiving service controls the data after delivery.

Use an endpoint that accepts your chosen method and parameters. GET and DELETE use query parameters; POST, PUT, and PATCH send a JSON object with string values. Optional custom headers support Authorization and API keys. Content-Type stays application/json; requests with custom headers refuse redirects.
Do rules send automatically as I browse?
No. Quick Send evaluates rules when you click the Hooky toolbar icon. The first enabled matching rule with a valid template sends. Otherwise, the popup opens.
Which page data can I use?
URL, title, selected text, description metadata, and Open Graph title, description, and image URL. Missing values become empty strings. Hooky does not extract the complete page body.
Does success mean my data is stored?

HTTP success confirms the HTTP response. An optional JSON business condition reflects the promise your receiver makes. Lost responses remain unconfirmed; Hooky does not retry automatically. Durable storage and idempotency need receiver support.

Headers, response reading, business rules, and completed duplicate protection are configured per webhook. Desktop notifications are a user preference. Clipboard access requires an explicit action and permission. Clear feedback and protection for sends already in progress apply to everyone.
